3_normalization.specificity_note: For this input, the hash cannot distinguish the lexer rule from rstrip()/strip(). The C++ discriminators show the rule is exactly 'pop one LF if the original ends in LF': x{{ a }}\n\n keeps one LF; a trailing space before LF is kept; a CRLF end is popped; a lone-CR end becomes LF and is NOT popped; leading whitespace is kept. The Python port matches C++ on all five cases, and rstrip()/strip() differ on them

root_criteria_verdict.justification: Judged against root's actual requirement, not the brief's added rival-hash sub-check. (a) The pinned C++ lexer (libllama-common.so sha 655f182f) turns the raw template into 6a1015c4..., and on 5 discriminator inputs it behaves as CRLF/lone CR -> LF plus removal of exactly one final LF when the original ends in LF. It is not rstrip/strip. (b) rstrip/strip give the same hash on this template only because the input cannot tell them apart (0 CR, 1 trailing LF, no leading whitespace); the evidence does not contradict the claim. (c) No other discrepancy: sources match the tarball, the GGUF template equals the raw template, no hacks apply, no override, backups verify, calls/semantics/ledger/exit 0/thinking off all check, and the host probe report equals the backup.
